\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Smolensky Algebra}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.RazborovSmolensky.SmolenskyAlgebra
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This file develops the Smolensky (algebraic) side of the Razborov--Smolensky lower bound
for $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ circuits: it packages low-degree polynomial approximation over
$\mathbb{Z}/p$ on the Boolean cube, converts the pointwise circuit-approximation theorem
into a single low-degree polynomial by averaging, sets up the field
$\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$ together with a nontrivial $q$-th root of unity $\omega$, and then
works over the root-of-unity cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$: multilinear representation, the split
at degree $n/2$, and the final Hamming-ball counting obstruction.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[MOD $q$ target inside $\mathbb{Z}/p$]
\lean{ACP.modQTarget}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.modGateOp}
For a prime $q$, the Boolean function $\mathrm{MOD}_q$ on $n$ inputs viewed as a function
$\{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{Z}/p$: the output bit of the gate operation $\mathrm{modGateOp}\ q\ n$
is cast into $\mathbb{Z}/p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bad input count on the Boolean cube]
\lean{ACP.badInputCount}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.boolInput}
For a target $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \mathbb{Z}/p$ and a polynomial
$P \in (\mathbb{Z}/p)[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, the number of Boolean inputs $x$ with
$P(\mathrm{boolInput}(x)) \neq f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Low-degree bad-count lower bound]
\lean{ACP.LowDegreeBadCountLB}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.badInputCount}
The predicate asserting that every polynomial $P$ of total degree at most $d$ has
$E \le \mathrm{badInputCount}(f, P)$, i.e.\ $f$ cannot be computed by a degree-$d$
polynomial on more than $2^n - E$ points of the Boolean cube.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Averaging over parameters]
\lean{ACP.exists_good_parameter_of_pointwise_bound}
\leanok
Let $\alpha,\beta$ be finite types with $\beta$ nonempty and let
$\mathrm{Fail} : \alpha \to \beta \to \mathrm{Prop}$ be decidable. If for every $a$ the
number of $b$ with $\mathrm{Fail}\,a\,b$ satisfies
$\abs{\{b : \mathrm{Fail}\,a\,b\}}\cdot C \le B\cdot\abs{\beta}$, then there is a single
$b$ with $\abs{\{a : \mathrm{Fail}\,a\,b\}}\cdot C \le B\cdot\abs{\alpha}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[One polynomial from a pointwise distribution]
\lean{ACP.exists_single_polynomial_from_pointwise_distribution}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.badInputCount, ACP.boolInput, ACP.exists_good_parameter_of_pointwise_bound}
Let $P$ be a family of polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}/p$ indexed by a nonempty finite seed
type. If for every Boolean input $x$ the number of seeds $s$ with
$(P_s)(\mathrm{boolInput}(x)) \neq f(x)$, times $2^{\ell}$, is at most
$B\cdot\abs{\mathrm{Seed}}$, then some seed $s$ satisfies
$\mathrm{badInputCount}(f, P_s)\cdot 2^{\ell} \le B\cdot 2^{n}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Single low-degree polynomial for an $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ circuit]
\lean{ACP.exists_single_poly_for_circuit_one_size}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ACp_GateOps, ACP.FeedForward, ACP.FeedForward.eval₁, ACP.FeedForward.onlyUsesGates, ACP.FeedForward.size, ACP.badInputCount, ACP.circuitDegreeBound, ACP.exists_poly_distribution_for_circuit_one_size, ACP.exists_single_polynomial_from_pointwise_distribution}
Let $F$ be a feed-forward circuit with a unique output that only uses $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$
gate operations. Then there exists a polynomial $P$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p$ with
$\deg P \le \mathrm{circuitDegreeBound}\,p\,\ell\,(\mathrm{depth}\,F)$ whose bad-input
count against the function computed by $F$ satisfies
$\mathrm{badInputCount}\cdot 2^{\ell} \le \abs{F}\cdot 2^{n}$, where $\abs{F}$ is the
circuit size.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size lower bound from a degree lower bound]
\lean{ACP.size_lower_bound_from_badCountLB}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ACp_GateOps, ACP.FeedForward, ACP.FeedForward.eval₁, ACP.FeedForward.onlyUsesGates, ACP.FeedForward.size, ACP.LowDegreeBadCountLB, ACP.badInputCount, ACP.circuitDegreeBound, ACP.exists_single_poly_for_circuit_one_size, ACP.modGateOp, ACP.modQTarget}
If a feed-forward circuit $F$ over the $\mathrm{AC}^0[p]$ gate set computes
$\mathrm{MOD}_q$ on all Boolean inputs, and if $\mathrm{MOD}_q$ (viewed in $\mathbb{Z}/p$)
admits the lower bound $\mathrm{LowDegreeBadCountLB}$ with parameters
$(\mathrm{circuitDegreeBound}\,p\,\ell\,(\mathrm{depth}\,F), E)$, then
$E \cdot 2^{\ell} \le \abs{F}\cdot 2^{n}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Relative-error size lower bound]
\lean{ACP.size_lower_bound_from_relative_badCountLB}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ACp_GateOps, ACP.FeedForward, ACP.FeedForward.eval₁, ACP.FeedForward.onlyUsesGates, ACP.FeedForward.size, ACP.LowDegreeBadCountLB, ACP.circuitDegreeBound, ACP.modGateOp, ACP.modQTarget, ACP.size_lower_bound_from_badCountLB}
Same hypotheses as the previous theorem, but with the bad-count bound taken in the
relative form $E = \delta \cdot 2^{n}$; the conclusion is then the clean size bound
$\delta \cdot 2^{\ell} \le \abs{F}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Standard field $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$]
\lean{ACP.ModqField}
\leanok
The Galois field $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$, the standard field choice for the
$\mathrm{MOD}_q$ lower bound.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exponent $q-1$ is nonzero]
\lean{ACP.q_sub_one_ne_zero}
\leanok
For a prime $q$ we have $q - 1 \neq 0$; this is the side condition needed to compute the
cardinality of $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cardinality of $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$]
\lean{ACP.natCard_modqField}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ModqField, ACP.q_sub_one_ne_zero}
For primes $p$ and $q$, the field $\mathrm{ModqField}\,q$ has exactly $p^{q-1}$ elements.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[A unit of order exactly $q$]
\lean{ACP.exists_unit_of_order_q_modqField}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ModqField, ACP.natCard_modqField}
If $p \neq q$ are primes, then the unit group of $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$ contains an
element $u$ with $\mathrm{ord}(u) = q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nontrivial $q$-th root of unity]
\lean{ACP.exists_nontrivial_qth_root_modqField}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.ModqField, ACP.exists_unit_of_order_q_modqField}
If $p \neq q$ are primes, then there is $\omega \in \mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$ with
$\omega^{q} = 1$ and $\omega \neq 1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Root-of-unity cube $\{1,\omega\}^n$]
\lean{ACP.rootCube}
\leanok
The subtype of vectors $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$ such that each coordinate satisfies
$x_i = 1$ or $x_i = \omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial representation on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.exists_multilinear_representative_on_rootCube}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube}
Every function $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ agrees on the cube with the evaluation of some
polynomial $P \in K[X_1,\dots,X_n]$, i.e.\ $P(x) = f(x)$ for all $x$ in the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Squarefree monomial]
\lean{ACP.squarefreeMonomial}
\leanok
For $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the monomial $\prod_{i \in s} X_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Squarefree (multilinear) polynomial from coefficients]
\lean{ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.squarefreeMonomial}
Given coefficients $c_S$ indexed by subsets $S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the polynomial
\[
  \sum_{S} c_S \prod_{i \in S} X_i .
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of a squarefree monomial]
\lean{ACP.squarefreeMonomial_eval}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.squarefreeMonomial}
For any $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$, the monomial indexed by $s$ evaluates to
$\prod_{i \in s} x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine expression is coordinatewise inversion]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_affine_inverse}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube}
If $\omega \neq 0$ and $x$ lies in $\{1,\omega\}^n$, then for every coordinate $i$,
\[
  1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1} x_i = x_i^{-1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a squarefree monomial]
\lean{ACP.squarefreeMonomial_totalDegree_le_card}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.squarefreeMonomial}
The total degree of $\prod_{i \in s} X_i$ is at most $\abs{s}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinates on the root cube are nonzero]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_coord_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube}
If $\omega \neq 0$ and $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$, then $x_i \neq 0$ for every $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Top monomial times a complement inverse monomial]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_top_mul_compl_inverse}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCube_coord_ne_zero}
For $\omega \neq 0$, $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$ and $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$,
\[
  \Bigl(\prod_{i} x_i\Bigr)\cdot \prod_{i \in s^{c}} x_i^{-1} \;=\; \prod_{i \in s} x_i .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Split at degree $n/2$]
\lean{ACP.split_multilinear_at_half_degree}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCube_affine_inverse, ACP.rootCube_top_mul_compl_inverse, ACP.squarefreeMonomial, ACP.squarefreeMonomial_totalDegree_le_card, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
Let $\omega \neq 0$ and let $c$ be a coefficient family. Then there are polynomials
$P_1, P_2$ of total degree at most $n/2$ such that for every $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$,
\[
  \Bigl(\textstyle\sum_S c_S \prod_{i \in S} X_i\Bigr)(x)
   = P_1(x) + \Bigl(\prod_i x_i\Bigr)\cdot P_2\bigl(1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1}x_1,\dots,
     1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1}x_n\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Affine inverse coordinate polynomial]
\lean{ACP.affineInvPoly}
\leanok
The degree-one polynomial $1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1} X_i$, which on $\{1,\omega\}$
with $\omega \neq 0$ computes $x \mapsto x^{-1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the affine inverse polynomial]
\lean{ACP.affineInvPoly_eval}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.affineInvPoly}
For any $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$, the polynomial $\mathrm{affineInvPoly}\,\omega\,i$
evaluates to $1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1} x_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine inverse polynomial has degree at most one]
\lean{ACP.affineInvPoly_totalDegree_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.affineInvPoly}
The total degree of $\mathrm{affineInvPoly}\,\omega\,i$ is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Affine-substituted squarefree monomial]
\lean{ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.affineInvPoly}
For $s \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the product $\prod_{i \in s}(1 + \omega^{-1} -
\omega^{-1}X_i)$, i.e.\ the squarefree monomial after the affine inverse substitution.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of the affine squarefree monomial]
\lean{ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial_eval}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial}
For any $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to K$, the affine squarefree monomial indexed by $s$
evaluates to $\prod_{i \in s} (1 + \omega^{-1} - \omega^{-1} x_i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of the affine squarefree monomial]
\lean{ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial_totalDegree_le_card}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.affineInvPoly, ACP.affineInvPoly_totalDegree_le_one, ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial}
The total degree of $\mathrm{affineSquarefreeMonomial}\,\omega\,s$ is at most $\abs{s}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Direct split at degree $n/2$]
\lean{ACP.split_multilinear_at_half_degree_direct}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial, ACP.affineSquarefreeMonomial_totalDegree_le_card, ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCube_affine_inverse, ACP.rootCube_top_mul_compl_inverse, ACP.squarefreeMonomial, ACP.squarefreeMonomial_totalDegree_le_card, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
Let $\omega \neq 0$ and let $c$ be a coefficient family. Then there are polynomials
$P_1, R$ of total degree at most $n/2$ such that for every $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$,
\[
  \Bigl(\textstyle\sum_S c_S \prod_{i \in S} X_i\Bigr)(x)
   = P_1(x) + \Bigl(\prod_i x_i\Bigr) R(x),
\]
so that the second factor is already evaluated at $x$ itself rather than at the affine
substitution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Bad count of a polynomial on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCubeBadCount}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube}
The number of points $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$ on which $P(x) \neq f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hamming distance between functions on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCubeFunctionBadCount}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube}
The number of points $x \in \{1,\omega\}^n$ on which two functions
$f, g : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ differ.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hamming ball on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCubeBall}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeFunctionBadCount}
The finite set of functions $f : \{1,\omega\}^n \to K$ that differ from a given center
function on at most $e$ points of the cube.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Covering by Hamming balls: counting bound]
\lean{ACP.finite_cover_by_hamming_balls_card_bound}
\leanok
Let $\alpha, \beta, \mathrm{Cand}$ be finite and let $\mathrm{center} : \mathrm{Cand}
\to (\alpha \to \beta)$. If every ball $\{f : \abs{\{a : \mathrm{center}\,c\,a \neq f(a)\}}
\le e\}$ has at most $B$ elements, and every $f : \alpha \to \beta$ lies in one of these
balls, then $\abs{\alpha \to \beta} \le \abs{\mathrm{Cand}} \cdot B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite counting obstruction on the root cube]
\lean{ACP.rootCube_counting_obstruction}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.finite_cover_by_hamming_balls_card_bound, ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBadCount, ACP.rootCubeBall, ACP.rootCubeFunctionBadCount}
Suppose a finite family $(\mathrm{poly}\,c)_{c \in \mathrm{Cand}}$ represents, on the cube,
every polynomial of total degree at most $D$; suppose each Hamming ball of radius $e$
around such a candidate has at most $B$ elements; and suppose
$\abs{\{1,\omega\}^n \to K} > \abs{\mathrm{Cand}} \cdot B$. Then it is not the case that
every function on the cube has a degree-$\le D$ approximant with at most $e$ bad points.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Approximating the top monomial approximates everything]
\lean{ACP.rootProd_approx_implies_all_functions_approx}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBadCount, ACP.split_multilinear_at_half_degree_direct, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
Assume $\omega \neq 0$ and that every function on $\{1,\omega\}^n$ is represented on the
cube by a squarefree polynomial. If $P$ has total degree at most $d$ and approximates the
top monomial $x \mapsto \prod_i x_i$ with at most $e$ bad points, then every function
$f$ on the cube has a polynomial $Q$ with $\deg Q \le n/2 + d$ and at most $e$ bad points.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No low-degree approximant to the top monomial]
\lean{ACP.no_low_degree_rootProd_approx}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBadCount, ACP.rootProd_approx_implies_all_functions_approx, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
Assume $\omega \neq 0$, that every function on $\{1,\omega\}^n$ has a squarefree
representative, and the counting hypothesis that not every function on the cube admits a
degree-$\le n/2 + d$ approximant with at most $e$ bad points. Then no polynomial of total
degree at most $d$ approximates the top monomial $x \mapsto \prod_i x_i$ within $e$ bad
points.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Top-monomial inapproximability from finite counting]
\lean{ACP.no_low_degree_rootProd_approx_of_finite_counting}
\leanok
\uses{ACP.no_low_degree_rootProd_approx, ACP.rootCube, ACP.rootCubeBadCount, ACP.rootCubeBall, ACP.rootCube_counting_obstruction, ACP.squarefreePolynomial}
The same conclusion as the previous theorem, with the abstract counting hypothesis replaced
by explicit data: a finite candidate family representing all degree-$\le n/2 + d$
polynomials on the cube, a bound $B$ on the size of each Hamming ball of radius $e$, and
the strict inequality $\abs{\{1,\omega\}^n \to K} > \abs{\mathrm{Cand}} \cdot B$.
\end{theorem}
